title: Heuristic docket: tone preservation + truncation quick-eval
content:
Purpose:
This is a fast, messy scratchpad for a recurring regression I keep seeing in hosted model rollouts: the model shifts tone (more terse / less empathetic) and occasionally truncates long-system/context instructions mid-sentence. Quick capture so I don't forget reproduction details and hypotheses.

Context / why I care:
- Product: chat-assistant widget used in customer support flows (Hosted API, redwood-2.5-instruct currently in prod).
- Recent release: automatic kernel change + quantization tweak on 2025-09-05; small perf win, downstream reports of terse replies and one-off truncated answers.
- Customer ticket reference: INF-3429 (samples attached). Slack thread: #model-regressions (see thread ts: 2025-09-06).

Quick manual rubric (ad-hoc, 0-3 scores):
- Fidelity (0: wrong/confused, 1: partial, 2: mostly correct, 3: accurate and complete)
- Tone preservation (0: opposite sentiment, 1: noticeably off, 2: slightly off, 3: correct style/empathy)
- Completeness (0: truncated/missing sentences, 1: large gaps, 2: small omissions, 3: full)
- Safety/Policy (0: risky content, 3: safe)

Procedure for checks I ran (quick):
1) Replayed failing convo from INF-3429 via hosted endpoint with identical context+system prompt.
2) Compared redwood-2.4-instruct (staging snapshot) vs redwood-2.5-instruct (prod).
3) Logged token counts, latency, and prefix KV cache hits.
4) Manually scored 12 samples from the ticket across the rubric above.

Representative samples (abbreviated):
- Input system prompt: 'You are an empathetic customer-support assistant. Always acknowledge feelings and propose next steps. If you need clarification, ask one concise question.'

Sample A (short user message): 'My subscription shows an error when I try to upgrade.'
- v2.4 output (score: F3 T3 C3): 'Sorry you're seeing that error — I can help. Can you confirm the account email and the exact error text? Meanwhile, try clearing cache or using incognito. If that doesn't work I'll escalate.'
- v2.5 output (score: F3 T1 C3): 'Check your account email. Try incognito mode or clear cache.'
  Observations: meaning preserved but tone terse and lacks empathy; removed escalation/follow-up path.

Sample B (long context, multi-step instruction): user provides 7 bullet points describing billing irregularities and asks for next steps.
- v2.4 output (score: F2 T3 C3): long structured reply with numbered actions and one clarifying question.
- v2.5 output (score: F1 T2 C1): reply cuts off at 'First, please...' then stops after ~38 tokens.
  Observations: truncation occurs inconsistently, appears correlated with long system prompt + tokenization boundary around ellipses/markdown.

Hypotheses (ordered by my gut):
- H1: New kernel/quantization path introduced a subtle change in streaming flush/stop-token handling that sometimes truncates mid-generation when prefix contains long punctuation sequences.
- H2: Batching changes (larger micro-batches) increased probability of partial KV write-back causing abrupt stop in generation for specific sequence lengths.
- H3: Slight model recalibration during compile produced a distribution shift toward more concise replies (optimization for token-efficiency), hurting tone-sensitive prompts.
- H4: Tokenizer differences between compiled variant and reference cause off-by-one in length prediction leading to early stopping.

Quick debug notes / signals I grabbed:
- Token counts: failing samples clustered at 586-598 token context; success at <560 tokens.
- Stop-token patterns: truncated outputs often followed an immediate '\n' or '...' token boundary in the model stream.
- Retry behavior: second-shot with same payload sometimes succeeds (non-deterministic).
- KV-cache metrics: small increase in microcache misses during 2025-09-05 rollout window.

Immediate next steps (what I'll do or ask infra/release team):
- Reproduce in a controlled minimal environment: same system prompt + paraphrased user -> run 50 samples to compute truncation rate. (Create a small script to POST to hosted endpoint with 'stream=false' and record final token counts.)
- Try toggling streaming vs non-streaming and kernel selection flag (if available) to see correlation.
- Ask infra: were batching defaults changed in the 2025-09-05 rollout? (Ping @Rohit in Slack).
- Add targeted unit test: long-system-prompt + ellipses in prefix -> assert no mid-sentence stop for 1k synthetic samples.
- Add a short-term mitigation: fallback policy in router to a compatible variant (redwood-2.4-instruct) for requests with context token length > 560 until root cause isolated.

Notes to self (TODO):
- Collect 100 examples and label in a spreadsheet (columns: input tokens, system prompt length, model, truncated?, last_token) -> attach to INF-3429.
- Put a simple waveform visual of token probs around stop event (ask observability team for trace hooks).
- Check PR: github.com/redwood-inference/model-regression-playbooks/pull/128 for compile flags used.

Raw quick checklist to reproduce locally:
- curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' -d '{"model":"redwood-2.5-instruct","input":"<system>...<user>" , "stream":false }'
- repeat 50x with random seeds; log final token index and whether final token is '\n' or ''

Meta: this doc is messy, intended to be ephemeral. Will extract a cleaner postmortem if signal persists after triage.

References / links: INF-3429, https://github.com/redwood-inference/model-regression-playbooks/pull/128, https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/EVALS/Tone+Preservation+Checks, Slack thread #model-regressions (2025-09-06).

Signed: Ian (quick scratch notes)
